title: Merging Gas-rich Galaxies That Harbor Low-luminosity Twin Quasars at z = 6.05: A Promising Progenitor of the Most Luminous Quasars
question: What are the gas content, star formation, dynamics and possible outflows of the host galaxies of a low-luminosity quasar-quasar pair at z = 6.05, and is the pair a progenitor of the most luminous quasars?

recipe.method: Pipeline-calibrated data re-imaged with CASA tclean (Briggs robust = 2.0); line-free channels give the continuum map; uvcontsub (first-order) removes continuum before the cube; channels averaged to 50 km/s
key_parameters: robust = 2.0; 50 km/s channels; 3 sigma clean depth

recipe.goal: measure [CII] fluxes, redshifts and line widths in apertures
recipe.method: Circular apertures (1.5'' diameter for C1, 1.0'' for C2 + Bridge and Tail, 6.0'' for the whole system) on the velocity-integrated map; single Gaussian fits to the spectra for redshift and FWHM

recipe.goal: derive [CII] luminosity, SFR and molecular gas mass
recipe.method: L_[CII] from flux via Solomon & Vanden Bout; SFR_[CII] from De Looze 2014 calibration; M_H2 ~ 30 L_[CII] from Zanella 2018
key_parameters: rest frequency 1900.5369 GHz; SFR calibration uncertainty factor of two
assumptions: [CII] excited primarily by star formation (SFRs are upper limits if quasar contributes)
Flat LCDM H0 = 70 km/s/Mpc, Omega_M = 0.3, Omega_Lambda = 0.7

recipe.goal: measure the FIR continuum and derive dust properties
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fit with imfit for position and size; modified blackbody (optically thin) gives L_FIR (42.5-122.5 um), L_TIR (8-1000 um), M_dust; SFR_TIR from Murphy 2011
key_parameters: T_dust = 35 K, beta = 1.6, kappa = 0.77 (850 um/lambda)^beta cm2/g
assumptions: T_dust = 35 K (local LIRG value, lower than the canonical 47 K for luminous quasars); beta = 1.6; CMB correction applied; TIR emission entirely from star formation; Kroupa IMF

recipe.goal: map global velocity field and estimate dynamical masses
recipe.method: Moment-1 (and moment-2) maps with immoments and 3.5 sigma clipping; beam-deconvolved imfit sizes give inclination from axis ratio; thin-disk M_dyn with D = 1.5 a_maj and V_circ = 0.75 FWHM/sin i
assumptions: [CII] emission arises from thin rotating disks; inclination from deconvolved axis ratio

recipe.goal: test for and quantify a [CII] outflow at C1
recipe.method: Fit the C1 spectrum (single synthesized beam) with single and double Gaussians (second centroid fixed to first); broad wing treated as outflow; M_out from L_[CII],broad with X_C+, T_ex; outflow rate M_out V_out / R_out; total rate = 3x neutral rate; mass loading factor = total outflow rate / SFR
key_parameters: X_C+ = 1.4e-4, T_ex = 200 K, high density limit (n >> n_crit ~ 3e3 cm^-3), R_out = 1.5 kpc, V_out = FWHM/2
assumptions: Wing is due to outflow (symmetric wing disfavors unseen companions); 70% of [CII] from neutral PDRs; constant outflow velocity
